verdict.rationale: Letta explicitly documents self-hosting: 'Letta agents can run entirely on infrastructure you control' and the App Server can be run on a central, always-on machine with all state staying on-device and no cloud account required (letta-docs-30, letta-docs-2/15/38, letta-docs-74, letta-docs-32, letta-docs-31). This confirms a platform engineer can run the memory/agent layer on owned infrastructure. However, the evidence never mentions Docker, docker-compose, or container images, nor explicitly confirms the App Server itself (vs. just the SDK) is distributed as open-source code — the GitHub repo evidence (letta-gh-1) only describes the TypeScript Agent SDK, not the server. Missing for 10: explicit Docker/container deployment instructions, confirmation the self-hosted App Server binary/source is open-source, and any independent verification of a successful self-hosted deployment.
